blocks.text: Chemical waste cannot be disposed of in bins or the sewer system. Most chemical wastes must be disposed of according to the rules and regulations of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA):

items: Store chemical wastes in proper containers.
Label the chemical waste containers with the type of waste, the date of the waste and the place of origin.

Transfer the containers to the allocated site where they are appropriately treated for disposal: chemical treatment of wastes involves neutralization, precipitation, ion exchange, oxidation or reduction.

blocks.caption: Chemical treatments of waste
rows: acid or alkali waste brought to a safe pH
dissolved harmful ions made insoluble and separated
harmful ions removed onto a resin
a harmful substance converted to a safer one

blocks.prompt: How is chemical waste disposed of (Quick Check 16.1b)?
blocks.explanation: Never into bins or the sewer: it is stored in proper containers, labelled with the type of waste, the date and the place of origin, and moved to the allocated site, where it is treated chemically by neutralization, precipitation, ion exchange, oxidation or reduction before disposal.

items: Chemical waste: never in bins or the sewer; store in proper containers, label (type, date, origin), transfer to the allocated site; treatment by neutralization, precipitation, ion exchange, oxidation or reduction (EPA rules).
